standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies that a finite central simple algebra has a separable splitting field, whose Galois closure is then also a splitting field, giving the chain to the matrix algebra conditions.

core_obligations: The first two conditions (proof lines 1005-1006): their equivalence is a consequence of the definitions, referring to the section on algebras.

From the first condition to the matrix algebra conditions (proof lines 1007-1011): the separable splitting field supplied by the cited proposition has a Galois closure which is a splitting field as well, and the chain of implications from the fifth to the fourth to the third condition is clear.

From the third condition back (proof lines 1012-1014): if the base change to the algebraic closure is a matrix algebra then it is central simple, which forces the algebra itself to be a finite central simple algebra.
The last condition (proof lines 1015-1017): the equivalence of the first and the sixth condition is Wedderburn's theorem.
proof_roadmap: Read the first equivalence off the definitions.
Go around the circle using a separable splitting field, its Galois closure, and the clarity of the two downward implications.
Return using that a base change of a matrix algebra is central simple, and close with Wedderburn's theorem.
difficulty_reason: The lemma collects six equivalent characterizations of a finite central simple algebra, including two matrix algebra conditions after extending scalars to the algebraic closure and to a separable closure, and the description via a finite central skew field (statement lines 984-1002). The proof is a complete argument: the first equivalence is a consequence of the definitions; the implication to the matrix algebra conditions uses the existence of a separable splitting field together with its Galois closure (proof lines 1007-1011); the converse direction uses that a base change of a matrix algebra is central simple (proof lines 1012-1014); and the last equivalence is Wedderburn's theorem (proof lines 1015-1017). The non-formal content is the arrangement of the circle of implications. The claim is H2.
